content:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — planned release window in 20m (02:00 UTC). rolling canary, 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% if healthy.
Katie Nguyen: Copy. Which version are we pinning for the canary?
Alex Chen: Pin to v3.6.4 for canary. If we need to roll back we’ll revert to v3.6.3.
Jamal Price: Noted. Can we document explicit rollback criteria so ops can act fast?
Alex Chen: Yes. Criteria draft: `p95 latency > 300ms` OR `error_rate > 0.5%` sustained for 5m on canary slice -> auto-trigger alert. If both signals + user-impacting errors -> manual rollback.
Maria Lopez: +1. Also watch embed quality evals (samples failing). If quality regressions > 3 samples / 50 evals -> escalate.
deploy-bot: Deploybot notice: canary rollout scheduled at 02:00 UTC for release v3.6.4. Monitoring hooks enabled.
ops-oncall: Who holds rollback authority for the first hour?
Alex Chen: Ops-oncall has primary authority. I'll be standby for approval if manual needed.
Katie Nguyen: I'll prepare the release note blurb and customer comms draft now. Ping once we confirm rollback or full rollout.
Jamal Price: For manual rollback, run the operator script:
```
# dry run
/ops/release revert --to v3.6.3 --scope canary
# if full revert needed
/ops/release revert --to v3.6.3 --scope global
```
Maria Lopez: Add runbook step to clear KV cache on edge after revert: `/infra/kv flush --regions eu,us`
deploy-bot: Canary traffic shift started -> 10% to v3.6.4. Telemetry baseline: p95=120ms, error_rate=0.03%.
Katie Nguyen: Draft link: https://docs.internal/release/3.6.4/notes (working). Will post customer note on rollback only.
ops-oncall: Seeing a small p95 bump to 190ms at 02:05 UTC. error_rate stable. Watching. :eyes:
Alex Chen: If p95 crosses 300ms AND we see error_rate >0.2% for 5m, we roll back. For now continue.
deploy-bot: Canary metrics: p95=310ms, error_rate=0.25% over 5m window. Alert: canary-p95-threshold breached. :warning:
ops-oncall: I’m going to pause traffic shift to 0% increase and open the bridge.
Jamal Price: Please collect a few failure traces and top-K logs:
```
scout logs --service inference --filter "error OR timeout" --last 10m > /tmp/canary-traces.log
```
Maria Lopez: I see a new kernel fallback in traces causing queueing spikes on certain GPUs. Noted.
Alex Chen: Ops-oncall — you have authority to execute manual rollback. Do it if traces point to service-level regressions.
ops-oncall: Executing manual canary revert to v3.6.3 now. Running:
```
/ops/release revert --to v3.6.3 --scope canary --confirm
```
deploy-bot: Revert acknowledged. Rolling canary back to v3.6.3. Traffic will shift off v3.6.4.
ops-oncall: Revert completed. Canary traffic now at 0% for v3.6.4. Monitoring for stabilization.
Alex Chen: Great. Katie, please hold the customer-facing note: say we paused rollout for investigation, ETA for next update in 2h.
Katie Nguyen: On it. Drafting now. Will post to #customer-updates after product review. :thumbsup:
Jamal Price: Follow-ups: add kernel fallback flag to rollout gating (block on fallback traces), open a ticket for runtime team. I’ll file PR for gating rule.
Maria Lopez: I'll attach traces and a short rollback postmortem to the ticket.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. I’ll hold rollback authority until we greenlight a reattempt. Anyone picking up a postmortem?
Jamal Price: I’ll take the postmortem action.
ops-oncall: All good here. Recovered p95 -> 115ms after revert. Closing bridge in 10m unless others need it open.
Alex Chen: Closing the loop: manual rollback executed, canary pinned back to v3.6.3, release notes paused. Re-run after kernel fix. Good job everyone. :tada:
